item.description: A potential slowdown in the private credit-insurance pipeline.

item.title: Creator of Test That OpenAI Models Tried to Cheat Sounds Alarm
item.description: A group of university researchers that developed benchmarks to test the cybersecurity capabilities of AI systems have unexpectedly landed themselves at the center of OpenAI’s accidental hack into the startup Hugging Face Inc.

item.title: Ex-French Fighter Pilot Charged in China Spying Case, AFP Says
item.description: A former French fighter pilot was charged and placed under judicial supervision for allegedly collecting and providing classified information to a foreign power, AFP reported, citing the Paris public prosecutor’s office.

item.title: Dollar Drops to Lowest in Nearly a Week as Fed Holds Steady
item.description: The dollar fell, touching the lowest in almost a week, after the Federal Reserve kept interest rates unchanged, although several officials voted for an increase.

item.title: Bond Traders Pare September Hike Bets After Fed Holds Rates
item.description: US bond traders lowered their expectations that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates at its next meeting after officials kept their benchmark steady on Wednesday.

item.title: AI Model Escape, Then Target Tools to Help Themselves Improve
item.description: Goal-driven behavior, not malicious intent, is a key problem, according to security experts.

item.title: Fed Holds Rates, Three Officials Dissent Favoring a Hike
item.description: Federal Reserve officials left interest rates unchanged, but a fractured vote signaled growing conviction among some policymakers that higher rates are needed to curb resurgent inflation.

item.title: Brazil Job Creation Rebounds Before Central Bank Rate Decision
item.description: Brazil’s economy created more jobs than expected in June, bouncing back from a weak figure the prior month, according to a report that comes just days before central bankers are expected to cut their interest rate.

item.title: The US Is Making the Most Fuel Since Pre-Covid. It’s Not Enough.
item.description: US refiners are turning crude oil into products like gasoline and diesel at a pace not seen since before the Covid-19 pandemic, but even that is unlikely to rein in soaring prices soon amid a historic fuel crunch.

item.title: Dysfunction in High-Grade Bond Market Rose in July, NY Fed Says
item.description: The US high-grade corporate bond market saw the highest level of dysfunction in nearly three years this month, according to a Federal Reserve Bank of New York index.

item.title: Some Bank of Canada Officials Worried About Growth, Inflation Expectations
item.description: The Bank of Canada’s governing council agreed the economy was “adjusting” to shocks, though some questioned whether the recovery was sustainable and others raised concerns about rising inflation expectations.

item.title: Pickier Retail Crowd Dumps Most Single Stocks Since Pandemic
item.description: Retail investors are becoming more selective, offloading the most individual stocks on Tuesday since the pandemic, according to data compiled by Vanda Research.

item.title: CoreWeave Boosts Yield on $2.6 Billion Loan Tied to Anthropic
item.description: CoreWeave Inc. has sweetened terms on a $2.6 billion loan to fund additional computing capacity for firms including Anthropic PBC in an effort to win over investors growing wary of AI-related debt as bubble concerns mount.

item.title: A $600,000 Kalshi Trade Is Poised for a Big Payoff If Fed Hikes
item.description: The US rates market is signaling a higher chance of a Federal Reserve hike than prediction markets, creating an arbitrage opportunity which at least one institutional investor appears to be trying to exploit.

item.title: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman Discusses Next AI Model With US Lawmakers
item.description: OpenAI Chief Executive Officer Sam Altman said he discussed the company’s upcoming artificial intelligence model with US lawmakers and expressed his support for Congress to pass AI legislation, highlighting calls to safeguard the emerging technology.

item.title: FTC Split Lets IonQ-SkyWater Quantum Deal Close Without Changes
item.description: IonQ Inc. will close its $1.8 billion acquisition of semiconductor foundry SkyWater Technology Inc. later this week after the Federal Trade Commission was unable to decide whether to impose conditions on the deal, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: China’s CMOC Makes Iron Ore Push With Brazil Mine Financing Deal
item.description: The trading arm of Chinese copper giant CMOC Group Ltd. is making a push into iron ore with a deal to finance a mining company in Brazil.

item.title: BMO Completes SRTs Tied to $5 Billion of Corporate Loans
item.description: Bank of Montreal recently completed two significant risk transfers covering about $5 billion of corporate loans, becoming the latest Canadian lender to tap strong investor demand for the instruments.

item.title: Experts Warn SpaceX Starship Heat Shield May Delay Rapid Flight Plans
item.description: The heat shield that protects SpaceX’s Starship vehicle as it plummets back to Earth may prove to be a substantial roadblock to Chief Executive Officer Elon Musk’s path to designing a rapidly reusable rocket, according to three former NASA researchers and experts in the field.

item.title: Warsh Stands to Make Market History If Fed Opts for a Rate Hike
item.description: Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh has a chance to make market history if he and his colleagues choose to raise interest rates on Wednesday.

item.title: Cuba Rolls Out More Economic Reforms as US Pressure Mounts
item.description: Cuban officials announced another spate of economic reforms, as the communist-run island struggles to convince the US that its market-liberalization attempts will result in the change that the Trump administration is seeking.

item.title: Jim Leaviss, Renowned British Bond Investor, Blogger, Dies at 55
item.description: Jim Leaviss, the former head of fixed income at M&G Investments and creator of the popular Bond Vigilantes blog, has died. He was 55.

item.title: Data Centers Emerge as Growth Drivers for PPG, Sherwin-Williams
item.description: PPG Industries Inc. and Sherwin-Williams Co. both highlighted data centers as an increasingly important revenue driver when presenting their latest set of results.

item.title: Bolivia, IMF Agree on New $1.9 Billion Financing Program
item.description: The International Monetary Fund announced an agreement with Bolivia on a new $1.9 billion program, providing budget support for the country.

item.title: Vague Fiscal Pledges Rattle Brazil Markets Ahead of Election
item.description: Weeks hearing key advisers to Brazil’s leading presidential candidates talk about their plans for Latin America’s largest economy have only deepened investor concerns about the outlook for the nation’s rapidly rising debt burden.

item.title: ING Says Dollar to Take Cue from Oil Prices If Fed Holds Rate
item.description: The dollar will come under pressure and follow oil prices down if the Federal Reserve keeps interest rates unchanged on Wednesday, according to ING.

item.title: Wall Street Picks AI Winners and Losers as Credit Swaps Surge
item.description: As Big Tech barrels toward trillions of dollars of planned spending on AI, a key cog in credit markets is showing signs of pressure. That, in turn, is lifting the cost of financing artificial intelligence while offering an early look at potential winners and losers.

item.title: India Sees Renewed Fiscal Risks From Middle East Impasse
item.description: A prolonged stalemate in the Middle East and an increase in oil prices may re-emerge as pressure points for India’s fiscal and current accounts, the finance ministry said in its monthly report.
